items.stem: Why use a multi-stage Dockerfile that builds with the SDK image but ships the runtime (or chiseled) image?

options.text: The final image is smaller and has a reduced attack surface, without build-time tooling
options.rationale: Correct: multi-stage builds keep SDK tooling out of the final image, shrinking size and attack surface.

options.text: The SDK image is always smaller than the runtime image
options.rationale: The SDK image is larger; that is why it is not shipped.
Runtime images are precisely for running .NET apps.

options.text: It is required to compile C#
options.rationale: Compilation needs the SDK, but shipping it is unnecessary; multi-stage separates the two.

items.explanation: Correct: multi-stage builds keep SDK tooling out of the final image, shrinking size and attack surface.

items.stem: Select TWO operational settings that improve a .NET workload running on Kubernetes.

options.text: Liveness and readiness probes so Kubernetes can restart or withhold traffic appropriately
options.rationale: Correct: probes let the platform self-heal and route traffic only to healthy pods.

options.text: CPU and memory requests/limits to guide scheduling and prevent noisy-neighbor issues
options.rationale: Correct: requests/limits inform scheduling and bound resource use.

options.text: Shipping the SDK image to production for flexibility
options.rationale: The SDK image is larger and widens the attack surface; use a runtime image.

options.text: Removing all health checks to reduce overhead
options.rationale: Removing probes prevents self-healing and safe rollouts.

options.text: Hard-coding a single replica with no scaling
options.rationale: A single fixed replica prevents scaling and resilience.

items.explanation: Correct: probes let the platform self-heal and route traffic only to healthy pods.

items.stem: In Kubernetes, what is the relationship between a Deployment and the pods it manages?

options.text: A Deployment declares the desired state and manages ReplicaSets that keep the right number of pods running
options.rationale: Correct: a Deployment manages ReplicaSets to maintain the desired pod count and handle rollouts.

options.text: A Deployment is a single pod with another name
options.rationale: A Deployment manages many pods via ReplicaSets; it is not one pod.
The relationship is the reverse: Deployments manage pods.

options.text: A Deployment is only a network load balancer
options.rationale: That role belongs to a Service, not a Deployment.

items.explanation: Correct: a Deployment manages ReplicaSets to maintain the desired pod count and handle rollouts.
